assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the proglucagon-derived peptide through its insulinotropic and satiety actions to long-acting agonists, has produced a new class of therapy that is transforming diabetes and obesity care. It is a rare case of mechanism, translation and very large patient benefit combined, with cardiovascular and renal outcome data accumulating.
assessment.attribution: The decisive scientific contributions are plausibly Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (biology and therapeutic translation, GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form). Knudsen is credited for industrial development of liraglutide and semaglutide, an engineering contribution that is harder to fit within three. Other pioneers, such as Habener, are not in the supplied credit and cannot be added, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical effects are independently confirmed in large randomized trials and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the global impact.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among academic discoverers and the drug-development contribution is unresolved.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history of the active peptide and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. The originality and clarity of the discovery-to-patient path are exceptional and the lasting impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Credit for the underlying BCR-ABL oncogene biology belongs to others outside this entry, which is a limit of the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data over two decades and many independent confirmations make this very mature. Recognition is well past due by timing alone, though the Lasker-level consensus suggests it remains highly competitive.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be framed around the targeted-therapy concept or the drug, and how earlier oncogene discoveries factor in.
Chemist and clinician roles may be weighed differently by the full Assembly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells have created durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now extend to myeloma and autoimmune disease. This is a new therapeutic modality with strong originality and rapidly growing impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the costimulatory-domain design and the first clinical successes in CLL and ALL. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR work, but credit for the original chimeric receptor concept (for example Eshhar) is not in the supplied names, so the configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is well replicated with multiple approved products, but long-term safety, solid-tumor limits and secondary malignancy signals remain under study. Recognition is timely and plausibly slightly early for the full story.
uncertainties: Absence of the original receptor-concept inventor from the credited names complicates fair attribution.
Long-term durability and safety are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signalling logic (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6 and PERK arms) and is central to proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and diseases such as diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The discovery is conceptually clear and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the established core pair, with Walter's work on Ire1 and Hac1 mRNA splicing and Mori's identification of the UPR pathway in yeast and mammals. Two laureates give a clean and fair configuration, with Ron Prywes and others at the margins.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is extensive and independent across eukaryotes, and the mechanism is stable. Direct clinical translation is still developing, but basic-science maturity is high.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation to patients is less advanced than in the clinical candidates ranked above.
The balance between basic cell biology and medical significance may be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is now ubiquitous in circuit research, with early clinical translation in vision restoration. It is a transformative tool with clear originality and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The credited set has six people, so a choice of three is forced. Nagel and Hegemann (and Bamberg) discovered and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden made them work in neurons; Miesenboeck pioneered an earlier genetically targeted light-control concept. Any trio omits a decisive contributor, and this is the key weakness.
assessment.maturity: The method is extensively replicated, though the clinical benefit is early and the prize would honour a research tool.
uncertainties: Attribution is highly contested and no three-person configuration is fully satisfactory.
As a neuropharmacologist I may be inclined to overvalue neuroscience tools, so I discount this deliberately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis and the demonstration of benefit from blockade opened the era of biologic therapy for chronic inflammatory disease, with application to Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. The impact on patients is large and well established.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini form a natural pair for the proof-of-concept in rheumatoid arthritis. The contributions of antibody engineers and of TNF cloning and biology work (for example by Cerami, Vilcek and others) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of clinical use and biosimilars. Recognition is long overdue rather than premature, though the target-validation story is well known and contained.
uncertainties: Credit for TNF biology and antibody production is spread beyond the two credited names.
Overlap with the Lasker award history may reduce perceived novelty to the Assembly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, transforming a fatal infant disease and validating splice-switching oligonucleotides as a modality.
assessment.attribution: Krainer provided the splicing-regulation mechanism and target identification, and Bennett the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development. This is a clean two-person configuration, though Ionis and Biogen clinical leaders and gene-therapy competitors are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Clinical benefit is replicated and long-term follow-up is accumulating over several years. The modality is still maturing and the field may become more compelling in a few years.
uncertainties: Competing SMA modalities (gene therapy, small-molecule splicing modifiers) may share recognition.
Industrial and academic credit weighting is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus changed the treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and led to wider neuromodulation. As a clinician in this area I see the practical effect on patients directly, although the therapy is symptomatic and not disease-modifying.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the clear originator of high-frequency stimulation in this context, with a single laureate configuration. Others, notably Delong and Limousin on the subthalamic target and basal ganglia model, are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed with decades of use. The recognition is overdue by timing, though it received a Lasker Award, which makes the case plausible.
uncertainties: Whether the Assembly would prefer to recognize the basal ganglia circuit model alongside the surgical technique.
The single-name credit omits contributions that some would call decisive.
